clue.text: It's quite a pull back to the lake

parts.note: surface padding that sets the scene and supplies no letters

indicators.note: going back means the phrase before it is read from its end to its start

parts.note: taken as written
a pull or tug is a drag

explanation.surface: A walker grumbles that the hike back up to the lake is a real slog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's quite' is scene-setting padding; the working part is 'a pull' turned round. Garda is the large lake in northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Garda is Italy's largest lake, so the name alone stands for that particular body of water.

clue.text: But they don't lie in some beds they make

definitions.text: But they don't lie in some beds they make

parts.words: But they don't lie in some beds they make
parts.note: surface reading: people who make a bed but never sleep in it, like hotel staff
setter's reading: the beds are flower beds dug and planted outdoors

explanation.walkthrough: Making a bed suggests sheets and pillows; the beds here are plots of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: People who tend plots dig and plant flower beds, yet nobody sleeps in that kind of bed.

clue.text: Split the head of the connecting bolt

parts.note: rive is an old verb meaning to split or tear apart

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A mechanic finds that a bolt joining two parts has cracked across its top.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivet is a metal pin hammered through plates to fasten them together, a kind of joining bolt.

clue.text: Self-control the governing principle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: control over one's own affairs, self-rule
second meaning: in ethics, the will laying down its own law

explanation.walkthrough: The Greek roots help: auto means self and nomos means law.
explanation.definitionFit: Independence of a state or person means ruling oneself, and in moral philosophy the will acting as its own lawgiver.

clue.text: Do they look proper too in a formal garden?

definitions.text: Do they look proper too in a formal garden?

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper
roses are the classic flowers of a formal garden

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether certain spring flowers would look neat enough in a formal garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the flowers while hinting at their two parts: prim and roses.
explanation.definitionFit: These pale yellow spring flowers are a familiar garden plant, and the question about looking proper fits their tidy appearance.

clue.text: Bridge support through holding ace

indicators.note: holding means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: per means through or by means of, as in per post
an ace is a one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An engineer explains that a bridge stays up because a strong support runs through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spans of a bridge rest on upright columns or piles, each one being a structural support.

clue.text: Like the bigot,. needs total inner reform

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded person needs a complete change of heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot refuses to accept people with different views or backgrounds, which describes being unaccepting.

clue.text: Vehicle for Communist propaganda in Cleveland ?

definitions.note: a place in Cleveland, not a description

parts.note: red is the traditional label for a Communist
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A loudspeaker van tours Cleveland spreading Communist propaganda.
explanation.walkthrough: A vehicle used for Communist propaganda would be a red car. Cleveland was a county in north-east England from 1974 to 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcar is a seaside town on the north-east coast of England that lay within the former county of Cleveland.

clue.text: This junction of course Italian

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the nickname of a tangled motorway interchange in Birmingham
second meaning: a pasta dish served as a course

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' reads as 'naturally' but means a course of a meal. Spaghetti Junction is the famous Gravelly Hill interchange on the M6 in Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin strands of pasta give their name to the knotted Birmingham road interchange and are an Italian dish.

clue.text: Beefy guide

definitions.note: adjective for a noun: a steer is a beef animal
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a young castrated bull raised for beef
second meaning: to direct or point the way

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like one phrase about a burly guide, but they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle farmers raise bullocks for meat, and to direct a vehicle or person is the verb sense.

clue.text: Facing always the wrong way, men in the race

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
taken as written

explanation.surface: Riders always seem to be facing backwards in this race.
explanation.definitionFit: A retaining wall or masonry layer protecting an embankment is called a facing, which is exactly what a revetment is.

clue.text: Once the most unpopular bird in Spain

definitions.text: Once the most unpopular bird in Spain

parts.note: surface reading: a bird species once hated by the Spanish
setter's reading: the bird is a male duck, and also the surname of the English sea captain who raided Spanish ships

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Drake attacked the Spanish fleet and treasure ships in the sixteenth century, so Spain loathed him.
explanation.definitionFit: A male duck shares its name with the Elizabethan privateer whom Spain regarded as its chief enemy.

clue.text: It's out of the Spanish wine area

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-works
tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a wine comes from the Spanish growing region.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe size or scope: the range a thing covers can be called its area.

clue.text: Man of the cloth whose work is colourless

definitions.text: Man of the cloth whose work is colourless

parts.note: surface reading: a clergyman whose sermons are dull
setter's reading: a textile worker who whitens fabric

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of the cloth' is the usual phrase for a priest; here the cloth is literal fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker in a textile mill who removes colour from linen or cotton fabric is described exactly this way.

clue.text: Monument gets damaged _ round one layer

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go around what follows
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a hen lays eggs, so it is a layer

explanation.surface: An ancient monument has been damaged around one of its layers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' looks like a stratum of rock; read it as something that lays, and it is a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric stone circle on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire is one of Britain's best-known ancient monuments.

clue.text: They reckon to find satire most upsetting

indicators.note: upsetting knocks things over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Critics reckon satire is the most upsetting form of comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: People who calculate or judge approximate costs or values are those who reckon figures.

clue.text: Ideal car for the company promoter

definitions.text: Ideal car for the company promoter

parts.words: Ideal car for the company promoter
parts.note: surface reading: a vehicle suited to a business executive
setter's reading: company as in the saying that two's company, so a promoter of intimacy for a couple

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd' turns company into a couple, not a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A small car with room for just driver and one passenger suits a couple who want privacy.

clue.text: Some excitement in the news
They are of service in Church or State

definitions.text: They are of service in Church or State

parts.note: surface reading: helpful people working for public institutions
setter's reading: the word names both clergy who lead services and government department heads

explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' does double duty: a church service and public service in government.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy who conduct worship and cabinet members running departments share the same title in Britain.

clue.text: Needed by lass with poor shoes?

definitions.text: Needed by lass with poor shoes?

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl or lass

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl whose shoes leak needs something to keep her feet dry.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a girl with leaky footwear needs waterproof overshoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber overshoes are pulled over ordinary footwear to keep them dry, just what worn-out footwear needs in wet weather.

clue.text: Put business in the way of a northerner

indicators.note: put in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put business obstacles in the way of a person from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland lies at the northern end of Great Britain, so its people are northerners from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: German Joiner in one race is overwhelming

definitions.note: a verbal noun: the act of overwhelming

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in means the first piece sits inside a later one

parts.note: a race or people is a nation
und is German for and, a joining word

explanation.surface: A German carpenter entering one race is overpowering everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter, but it is a word that joins, a conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: A flood swamps the land, and figuratively being swamped by too much of something is the same idea.

clue.text: Arabian spirit. Abroad consumed maybe nine

indicators.note: something consumed is swallowed, so it ends up inside

parts.note: je is French for I, a word used abroad

indicators.note: maybe signals one possible version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Arabian spirit swallowed perhaps nine people abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed full stop has probably swallowed an 'I': read 'I abroad', which is the French je.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinnee or genie is a supernatural being of Arabian folklore, the spirit of the lamp tales.

clue.text: Vision of a seer

parts.note: surface reading: a prophet's mystical vision of the future
setter's reading: a seer is simply an organ that sees, and its vision is its power to see

explanation.walkthrough: 'Seer' and 'vision' sound mystical, but both can be taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The ability to see with the eyes is literally the vision of the organ that sees.

clue.text: Many have a passing interest in them

definitions.text: Many have a passing interest in them

parts.note: surface reading: lots of people are casually curious about something
setter's reading: students want to pass these tests

explanation.walkthrough: A passing interest usually means fleeting curiosity; here it is the hope of passing.
explanation.definitionFit: Students sit formal tests at school or university and are keen to achieve a pass mark.

clue.text: They get drunk, like, in drams

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits, like a dram
as means like

explanation.surface: Some people get drunk on a few drams of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They get drunk' suggests drinkers; it is the toasts that are drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: When guests raise glasses and drink to someone's health, each salute is drunk in turn.

clue.text: Dressing for cheek

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a liquid condiment poured over food
second meaning: impudence or insolent talk

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a bandage for a face; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A condiment such as gravy or salad dressing, and British slang for impertinence, share the same word.

clue.text: Flying blind ? Must be crazy!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: nocturnal animals that fly by echolocation, proverbially blind

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is someone piloting without instruments; the first part describes flying mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: These winged mammals are proverbially blind, and colloquially someone barmy or mad is described this way.

clue.text: Encouragement to Thespians in London

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a call urging actors to perform, split as two words

definitions.note: a place in London, not a description
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a district of west London

explanation.walkthrough: Thespians are actors, so 'act on!' urges them to keep performing. Acton is a district in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: The suburb in the borough of Ealing in west London is spelt the same as the phrase urging actors forward.

clue.text: Farm building no use without beat anyway

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the first phrase surrounds the next

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: anyway means in any order you like, so the letters may be rearranged

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying round, as is a beat in some races; the printed beat may well be a misprint for heat

explanation.surface: A farm building is useless without some heating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking. Neat is an old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an old word for cattle, so a shed where cattle are housed is a farm building.

clue.text: Charming type of female cup-holder, say?

indicators.note: say means the words are to be spoken and heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a saucer holds a cup, and the feminine ending makes it a female saucer

explanation.surface: Someone describes a charming woman who holds a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming' looks like delightful, but it means casting charms or spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who works magic casts charms and spells, so she is a charming type in the literal sense.

clue.text: But in flight they're stationary

parts.note: surface reading: something airborne that somehow does not move
setter's reading: a flight of stairs is made of fixed treads that never move

explanation.walkthrough: A flight suggests travel through the air; a flight of stairs stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase, called a flight, is made up of individual treads that stay fixed in place.
